name: Mutton Yakhni
subtitle: pale yogurt and fennel mutton curry, aromatic rather than hot

ingredients.qty: 700g on the bone, cut into 4cm pieces
ingredients.note: shoulder or leg; the bone makes the stock
use compounded-free hing to keep the dish gluten-free

ingredients.qty: 1 tbsp dried, crushed between the palms

prepNotes: Whisk the yogurt with 2 tbsp water until there is not a single lump, and leave it on the counter for 30 minutes. Cold, grainy yogurt splits the moment it meets a hot pan.
This is Kashmiri Pandit cooking: no onion, no garlic. Everything rests on fennel, dry ginger and a pinch of hing, so use fresh stock of all three — year-old fennel powder tastes of dust.
Take the mutton out of the fridge 30 minutes ahead so it does not seize when it hits the ghee.

steps.text: Bring the mutton, water, bay leaves, black cardamom, cloves, cinnamon and 1 tsp salt to a boil, then skim off every bit of grey foam.
steps.tip: Skim properly now or the finished yakhni will be cloudy instead of ivory.

steps.text: Cover and simmer 40 minutes, until the meat gives easily to a fork. Lift the pieces out and keep the strained stock.
Heat the ghee in a heavy pan and add the hing — it foams and smells sharp for about 10 seconds.
Pull the pan off the heat and stir in the fennel powder and dry ginger for 20 seconds.
steps.tip: Off the heat: ground fennel scorches in seconds and turns bitter.

steps.text: Return to a low flame, add the drained mutton and turn it in the spiced ghee for 3 minutes until every piece is glossy.
Take the pan off the heat again, pour in the whisked yogurt and stir without stopping for 2 minutes before setting it back on the lowest flame.
steps.tip: Keep stirring in one direction until the yogurt is hot through; stop early and it breaks into grains you cannot rescue.

steps.text: Add 450ml of the reserved stock, the crushed mint and the black pepper, and simmer uncovered 20 minutes until the gravy thinly coats a spoon.
Crush the green cardamom over the top, check the salt and rest 10 minutes off the heat before serving with plain rice.

storage: Keeps 3 days refrigerated and tastes better on the second day. Reheat on the lowest possible flame while stirring; a hard boil will split the yogurt.
